items.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
items.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wants to defy the polls, and his main rivals accuse him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal".

items.title: Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
items.description: The headquarters of Halk TV were raided last month, the latest in a series of crackdowns on news sources deemed critical of the government.

items.title: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
items.description: The pilot was the sole survivor of the crash during a rescue mission in a remote area known for drug trafficking.

items.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
items.description: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.

items.title: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
items.description: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.

items.title: 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
items.description: Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.

items.title: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
items.description: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia has not.

items.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
items.description: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

items.title: Italy's former police chief rejected mafia inquiry allegations before death
items.description: The contents of an eight-page letter by Gianni De Gennaro have been revealed days after his body was found at his Tuscany home.

items.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
items.description: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing his followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

items.title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
items.description: The endangered reptiles were bound with duct tape to prevent them moving, officials say.

items.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
items.description: Hundreds of thousands of people were without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

items.title: 'It's impossible': Spain's young people on housing ahead of Sunday's election
items.description: Europe correspondent Nick Beake speaks to one couple kept apart by high rents in Valencia.

items.title: Zelensky questions 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
items.description: The Ukrainian president tells the BBC that Russia's Vladimir Putin should not be treated as a friend.

items.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
items.description: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

items.title: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
items.description: Hundreds of thousands have been affected by storms in the country as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend begins.

items.title: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
items.description: Ukraine settles in for another devastating winter as the questions persists: how will it all end?

items.title: Behind China's spectacular rise, voices who defied it say they are being drowned out
items.description: China's immense clout now also has the flex of soft power. Critics and dissidents say their voices are being drowned out.

items.title: A clinic is reassessing people with ADHD and autism diagnoses - but critics fear it could deepen stigma
items.description: While many people find a diagnosis for ADHD or autism affirming, a government-funded clinic in Sweden is re-assessing people who feel it does not reflect them.

items.title: The Indian 'Tamasha queen' whose fans paid for a show that never happened
items.description: A new Bollywood flim spotlights the remarkable life of dancer and singer Vithabhai Narayangaonkar.
